My thinking this year:

I farm 10.1 mu, wheat and maize both seasons like everyone here in Quzhou. Last year wheat gave me about 480 kg/mu, maize around 600 kg/mu — decent, not the best in the village. Li from the next plot got 520 on wheat because he added a bit more urea at jointing, so I will do similar this year.

For **wheat** (sown October, about 6 mu wait — no, I plant the full 10.1 mu both seasons since it's rotation):
- I buy improved seed from the town dealer, Jimai 22 or similar — everyone around me uses it, reliable for our soil.
- Base fertilizer: one bag of compound (15-15-15, 50kg) per mu at plowing, plus some DAP. That gives me roughly N 12, P 10, K 8. Then topdress urea at jointing — about 15 kg/mu (gives another N 7). Total N around 19-20 kg/mu. Fertilizer is expensive now, almost 160 yuan a bag, but I cannot cut it or yield drops.
- Irrigation: 3 times — before winter (dong shui), returning green (fan qing), and jointing. Well water, I pay electricity.
- Pesticide: 2 sprays — one for weeds in spring, one combined spray for aphids and powdery mildew before heading.
- Rotary till after maize harvest, straw returned.

For **maize** (sown June after wheat harvest):
- Hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 type, what the dealer pushes and neighbors use.
- Direct seeding no-till into wheat stubble, save time and diesel. One bag compound 15-15-15 as base, then topdress urea 15 kg at big trumpet stage. Total N about 22, P 8, K 7.
- Summer rains usually enough, but I irrigate once at tasseling if dry — last July was dry so I pumped once.
- One pesticide spray for corn borer, sometimes two if worms are bad.

My wife helps, my older son works in Handan city so we hire a little help at wheat harvest. I keep some margin on fertilizer — running short costs more than overspending.
